title: Zoom in: one leader per partition, chosen by the controller quorum
caption: Leaders are spread so writes are spread; when a broker fails, an in-sync follower takes over, and a returning broker has to catch up before it leads again.

steps.text: Three of flight-status's partitions, each with 3 replicas. The KRaft controller quorum records who leads each one and spreads the leaders: every broker leads one partition and follows the other two.
The flight-ops producer caches the leader map from metadata and sends each partition's batch straight to its leader, so the writes are spread over all three brokers.
Followers pull from the leader. For p2, brokers 1 and 2 fetch from broker 3; while they keep up they belong to p2's in-sync replica set (ISR).
With acks=all and min.insync.replicas=2, broker 3 acknowledges a batch only when every ISR member has it. Consumers read up to that point (the high watermark), never beyond.

scenarios.name: Broker 3 loses power
scenarios.summary: An in-sync follower takes p2 over within seconds and no acknowledged record is lost, but one broker now carries two partitions' writes.

steps.text: Broker 3 goes dark. It led p2 and held follower copies of p0 and p1.
Its session with the controllers expires after a few seconds. The controller picks broker 1 from p2's ISR as the new leader and bumps p2's leader epoch.

The producer gets NOT_LEADER_OR_FOLLOWER, refreshes its metadata and retries p2 on broker 1. Every acknowledged record was already there, and the idempotent producer keeps the retry from writing a duplicate.
Broker 2 now fetches p2 from broker 1. The ISR is {1, 2}, still enough for min.insync.replicas=2, but broker 1 takes the writes of two partitions until broker 3 is back.

scenarios.name: Broker 3 catches up
scenarios.summary: A returning broker is only a follower until it has every record; then the preferred leader election gives it p2 back.

steps.text: Broker 3 restarts. Using the leader epochs, it truncates any records it wrote that the new leader never had, then fetches everything it missed from broker 1.
When it reaches the end of broker 1's log, the leader adds it back: p2's ISR is {1, 2, 3} again.
Broker 3 is p2's preferred leader (first in its replica list), so the automatic leader rebalance moves p2 back. The producer retries once on NOT_LEADER and the writes are spread again.

scenarios.name: ISR shrinks to one
scenarios.summary: Followers that fall behind leave the ISR; with one replica left, acks=all refuses writes instead of accepting records that only one disk holds.

steps.text: Broker 1's disk slows down. It stops keeping up with p2, and after replica.lag.time.max.ms the leader drops it: the ISR is {3, 2}. Writes continue, one failure away from trouble.
Then broker 2 loses its network link. p2's ISR is just {3}.
With min.insync.replicas=2, broker 3 answers NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS: flight-ops can't publish p2's status changes and keeps retrying. p0 and p1 have their own ISRs and may still work.

If broker 3 died now, unclean leader election (off) keeps p2 offline rather than promote a stale copy that would drop acknowledged gate changes. An under-replicated-partitions alert at the first step is the real fix.
